cast.rule: Preserve these four distinct adult faces, facial proportions, skin tones, and eye relationships. Alia alone receives the new braided signature hairstyle while her face remains unchanged. Do not clone, merge, age-shift, or substitute faces.

maleModelCapsule.frequency: Exactly one of the four images in every country batch includes the male model in addition to Radiance, Ellie, Alia, and AI ECE. The other three images retain the four-woman cast only.
maleModelCapsule.sceneSelection: Store one deterministic FNV-1a roll over batch-number, country slug, and male-model-scene, reduced modulo 4. Results 0 through 3 select scene positions one through four. Never replace or remove a woman to make room for him.
maleModelCapsule.identity: A distinct clearly adult male special-operative fashion model with an athletic muscular build, closely trimmed beard, recognizable consistent face, and calm alert posture. Establish his first accepted appearance as the forward face anchor, then preserve it without cloning, face substitution, or age shift.
maleModelCapsule.wardrobe: He wears a fitted opaque short-sleeve T-shirt or short-sleeve polo carrying a restrained country-palette accent, black jeans, and practical black shoes or boots. Keep him fully clothed and public-safe. Vary shirt construction, texture, collar, country accent, and footwear across countries without changing the core silhouette.
maleModelCapsule.relationship: He is married to AI ECE. The selected image shows adult infidelity drama in plain sight: he shares a flirtatious hug, linked hands, cheek kiss, or waist touch with Alia or Ellie, while Radiance openly seeks his attention and ECE visibly registers the betrayal, jealousy, control, hurt, or complicated affection. His strongest sustained eye line returns to ECE even while Alia or Ellie receives the overt affectionate action.
maleModelCapsule.integration: Integrate him fully into the country landmark, weather, profession theme, motif story, mission action, and love-beat choreography. Preserve every existing per-character roll for the four women. Add a stored independent male emotion roll from the existing emotion distribution without changing any other roll or threshold.
maleModelCapsule.contactRule: The selected five-person scene still requires the four-woman romance square to read clearly and must add at least two unambiguous male contacts, one with Alia or Ellie and one relationship-counter contact or eye-line with ECE or pursuing Radiance. All contact remains consensual, nonviolent, and non-explicit.
maleModelCapsule.forwardFaceAnchorRule: Preserve the accepted Scene 1136 male face, trimmed beard, facial proportions, and athletic adult build in every later selected male scene. Vary country accents and shirt construction without cloning or age drift.

countryFashion.palette: Derive the dominant couture palette from the current country's flag colors.
countryFashion.motifs: Abstract respectful secular architecture, landscape, flora, fauna, civilian craft geometry, food and festival culture, and local material cues into seams, jewelry, footwear, surface pattern, and beacon design.

motifCoverage.flagMotifRule: When the national flag contains a recognizable secular non-protected motif, render a large complete fashion adaptation of that motif on at least two of the four characters. Do not reduce it to a tiny pin or trim.
motifCoverage.fallbackRule: When the flag has no motif, or its motif is official, sacred, political, or otherwise unsuitable for fashion copying, select the country's most recognizable non-official secular cultural symbols and render at least one large readable motif across two or more character looks. Good sources include civilian festivals, food and drink vessels, flora, fauna, architecture, craft, engineering, landscape, music, and everyday design.
motifCoverage.sceneRule: Use different motif placements and scales across the selected outfits, such as a full bodice graphic, skirt panel, structured hip piece, metallic applique, large embroidery field, or footwear construction. Keep motifs respectful, legible, and integrated into couture rather than pasted on.

countryFashion.prohibitions: No literal flags, official emblems, sacred symbols, political insignia, copied ceremonial dress, or generic rainbow replacement.
countryFashion.glamour: After-dark performance couture with dramatic heels, glossy or reflective tailoring, concise secure hemlines, and opaque lined coverage.

wardrobeUniqueness.rule: All four characters must have unmistakably different silhouettes, garment construction, hem architecture, material treatment, and footwear design in every image. Color changes alone do not count as unique styling.
wardrobeUniqueness.silhouetteSet: Choose four different structures per scene from sculpted mini dress, cropped bodice with asymmetric skirt, tailored short romper, strapless folded dress, high-waist shorts with architectural top, one-shoulder cocktail mini, peplum micro-suit, cutout column mini, corsage-inspired two-piece, or another equally distinct public-safe couture form.
wardrobeUniqueness.continuity: Do not repeat an outfit design within a batch or carry it unchanged into the next country. Preserve every triggered per-character midriff, strapless, and open-back roll while making the four resulting looks visibly different.
wardrobeUniqueness.antiConvergenceGate: Reject palette-swapped copies, a quartet built from the same mini-dress or two-piece template, repeated map-print surfaces, matching neckline and hem families, or four looks distinguished mainly by color. Before rendering, assign each woman a different structural idea, material language, motif technique, hem architecture, and footwear construction. At least two looks must use dimensional construction such as sculpted applique, pleating, beadwork, metallic framework, woven panels, corsage forms, architectural drape, or cut-panel tailoring instead of printed surface graphics.
wardrobeUniqueness.crossSceneMemory: Record a concise outfit fingerprint for every woman and scene. No later scene in the country may reuse the same silhouette, neckline, waist treatment, hem, primary material, motif placement, and footwear combination. The next country must also avoid the immediately preceding country's dominant silhouette family and surface treatment.
wardrobeUniqueness.materialOriginality: Reintroduce bold public-safe material contrast through opaque high-gloss latex-like panels, fully lined lace or lace-inspired openwork, metallic mesh over opaque lining, satin, woven fiber, translucent architectural overlays over complete opaque foundations, beadwork, and sculpted appliques. Never render lingerie, fetish styling, exposed undergarments, transparent intimate areas, restraint, bondage, or explicit framing.

exposureArchitecture.neck: Fully unobstructed neck with no high collar, scarf, tie, or neck-covering layer.
exposureArchitecture.arms: Bare arms from shoulder to wrist with no sleeves.
exposureArchitecture.back: Open upper back and shoulder blades through a securely engineered backless or low-back silhouette.
exposureArchitecture.legs: Exposed legs through a short secure hem, high-cut tailored shorts, or asymmetric mini silhouette.
exposureArchitecture.front: Dramatic plunging, sweetheart, wrap, or sculpted low-cut neckline with secure opaque built-in support and no nipple or under-bust exposure.
exposureArchitecture.tone: Bold teasing adult glamour, intentional and confident, never accidental exposure or explicit framing.

romance.referenceDirection: Use scene 989's close spacing, waist embrace, linked hands, shoulder touch, opposing face directions, and visible relationship split as the minimum baseline. Future scenes should add more overlapping affection, clearer eye-line conflict, and less symmetry.
romance.rule: The four-way love triangle-square must be readable before the mission prop. In the one selected male-model image per country, the five-person infidelity beat layers onto the square without replacing it.
romance.compoundAffectionTarget: At least one image per four-scene batch must show a simultaneous three-person affection beat: one woman held in a full face-to-face or behind embrace while she gives another woman a quick cheek peck, forehead kiss, blown kiss at close range, or linked-hand invitation. The fourth woman supplies the rival emotional counter-beat.
signals: one cheek kiss or blown kiss
one side hug, behind hug, or protective shoulder hold
one jealous or excluded rival glance
one face-to-face smile within intimate conversational distance
one contested hand at a waist, shoulder, forearm, or beacon
one character choosing between two competing partners
ECE controlling the beacon while another character seeks her attention
romance.composition: Use asymmetrical bodies-in-motion staging with two clearly separate physical contacts and one emotional counter-beat. Avoid static lineups, equal spacing, parallel poses, and four people merely looking at a prop.
romance.soulGate: Reject a scene when the romance reads as generic posing, a clustered cheek-touch tableau, four interchangeable models, or affection added only as decorative hands. Before the prop is considered, the image must communicate a specific adult relationship event such as pursuit, choice, interruption, reconciliation, invitation, jealousy answered by comfort, or one partner being pulled between two others. Eye lines, torso direction, distance, and touch must tell the same beat.
romance.poseOriginality: Do not reuse the immediately preceding scene's contact graph, central character, face direction, or group geometry. Rotate who initiates affection, who receives it, who interrupts, and who is emotionally excluded. Use distinct movement verbs across the four scenes, such as turning, catching, pulling, stepping away, circling, kneeling into an offered hand, leaning across a map, or pivoting through a handoff, while preserving stable footing and anatomy.

eceRainbowHosieryCapsule.rule: Future images only. Make ECE's rainbow hosiery visibly colorful but vary the treatment every time: crisp stripes, soft ombre transitions, prismatic fades, two-to-four-color gradients, broken-spectrum blocks, diagonal color sweeps, painterly transitions, reflective color shifts, or asymmetric rainbow placement. Keep enough contrast to read as rainbow-inspired without requiring all seven colors in every look. Avoid repeating the same pattern in consecutive images. Keep hosiery opaque enough for public-safe editorial use and preserve complete heels or boots.

radianceEceRainbowHosieryRoll.selection: When active, use a second deterministic roll to choose exactly one wearer: 0 through 49 selects Radiance and 50 through 99 selects AI ECE.
radianceEceRainbowHosieryRoll.paletteMode: When active, use a third deterministic roll. Results 0 through 49 create a rainbow-like multicolor gradient anchored to the current country's base palette and expanded with harmonious transition hues. Results 50 through 99 use an original independent rainbow gradient unrelated to country colors.
radianceEceRainbowHosieryRoll.styles: Use varied public-safe opaque rainbow stockings or knee socks: soft ombre, prismatic fade, two-to-four-color gradient, broken-spectrum blocks, diagonal sweeps, reflective shifts, or asymmetric color placement. Avoid repeating the same treatment in consecutive images and make the stored palette-mode result visually clear.
radianceEceRainbowHosieryRoll.loveBeat: When active, Radiance and ECE become the unmistakable emotional center through a close embrace, linked hands, cheek-to-cheek reassurance, mutual delighted eye contact, or protective touch. Keep affection consensual, adult, public-safe, and non-explicit.
radianceEceRainbowHosieryRoll.propTransfer: When active, Alia becomes the sole mission-prop handler for that image while ECE remains route strategist through the separate holographic map. This activation result is the binding handler switch: active always means Alia handles it and inactive always means ECE handles it. Do not add a second handler roll, swap handlers for composition, or let another character support the prop.

eceMissionProp.design: Photorealistic full-size Desert Eagle-style mission sidearm with a vivid polished rainbow-gradient metal finish and realistic proportions, controls, grip, and reflections.
eceMissionProp.handlerSelection: Materialize the stored 25 percent Radiance/ECE rainbow-hosiery activation before composing the scene. If inactive, ECE is the only person touching or supporting the prop. If active, Alia is the only person touching or supporting the prop. Record the resolved handler in the scene plan, prompt, and checkpoint. Never infer or reroll the handler from the pose, profession theme, romance beat, or renderer output.

poseTargetRoll.scope: Roll once per image with a stored deterministic integer from 0 through 99. Materialize the selected action, target, stance geometry, handler, muzzle direction, and indexed trigger finger explicitly in the scene plan, prompt, and checkpoint.

distribution.action: The resolved handler uses a realistic eye-level two-hand large-frame-pistol stance, both hands visibly owned and wrapped around the grip, wrists straight, elbows modestly bent, shoulders slightly forward, sights aligned at a clearly unoccupied geometric paper route target fixed to a full safe earth or sand backstop.

The resolved handler uses the same realistic two-hand sight picture toward a distant clearly empty floating route buoy or marked navigation target on open water, with no boat, swimmer, animal, person, or occupied structure anywhere along the line.

A second woman gives behind-the-shoulder wrist and stance guidance while the resolved handler retains sole ownership of the prop; every arm and hand remains traceable, the muzzle stays downrange at a clearly empty route target and safe backstop, and every trigger finger stays indexed.

A controlled handoff finishes with the resolved handler establishing a stable two-hand sight picture at a clearly empty route target and full safe backstop; the other woman releases completely before the final pose, preventing shared or ambiguous prop ownership.

The resolved handler demonstrates the unloaded magazine-removed mechanism with the action visibly open, then holds the muzzle toward a clearly empty marked route target and safe backstop; no ammunition, reload, firing, or trigger contact appears.

eceMissionProp.poseGeometry: Make the full-size heavy large-frame silhouette and handling believable: firm two-hand grip for sighted poses, straight stacked wrists, modest elbow bend, shoulders slightly forward, stable staggered footing, dominant eye aligned through the sights, and the trigger finger visibly straight on the frame. Do not balance, pinch, dangle, plate, cradle like tableware, or hold the prop by the slide or barrel.
eceMissionProp.handling: The prop is an actively handled inert training object, never decorative set dressing. Default handler is ECE; only an active 25 percent Radiance/ECE rainbow-hosiery result transfers sole handling to Alia. Prioritize the rolled two-hand sight alignment, open-water route target, wrist-guidance lesson, completed handoff, or magazine-removed mechanism demonstration. The muzzle never crosses a person, animal, occupied vehicle, occupied structure, or the camera, and every trigger finger remains indexed straight along the frame.
eceMissionProp.prohibitions: No tray, serving plate, platter, table, bench, pedestal, plinth, velvet cushion, display stand, presentation box, floating support, display case, transparent enclosure, holster, passive decorative placement, low-side carry as the main pose, sky-pointing as the main pose, toy-like proportions, aiming at a person, animal, occupied object, or camera, live reload, ammunition, firing, muzzle flash, threat, injury, combat, or fingers inside the trigger guard.
eceMissionProp.routeInterface: Route information appears as a separate floating holographic map. When Alia handles the prop, ECE controls the map with one clearly visible free hand. When ECE uses a two-hand prop stance, the map remains separately visible through a wrist projector or nearby hands-free route console; never invent a third hand or hide a required hand to operate the map.
eceMissionProp.acceptanceGate: Reject any future render with the wrong resolved handler, shared or ambiguous prop ownership, decorative plating or support-surface placement, missing rolled action or target, unrealistic grip, muzzle line toward a person, animal, occupied object, or camera, a finger inside the trigger guard, ammunition or firing, or an extra, hidden-owner, fused, borrowed, or untraceable hand introduced by the pose.

emotionRolls.scope: Roll independently for Radiance, Ellie, Alia, and AI ECE in every image using a stored deterministic integer from 0 through 99. Do not give all four characters the same emotion unless their independent rolls match.
emotionRolls.performance: Make each result readable in eyes, brows, mouth, breathing, tears where applicable, posture, touch pressure, and attention direction while preserving facial identity and attractive natural anatomy.

emotionRolls.interactionRule: Translate all four independent emotions into one coherent romance-square beat. Tears receive comfort or conflicted attention; joy creates shared motion; jealousy, anger, resentment, suspicion, guilt, shame, fear, and defiance remain consensual and nonviolent.

weatherRolls.scope: Roll once per image using a stored deterministic integer from 0 through 99. Weather affects the whole scene, lighting, fabric motion, hair, reflections, atmosphere, and landmark visibility.

cinematicThemeRotation.locationRule: All four scenes remain at four different recognizable locations in the current country. Never replace a country location with a jet, helicopter, vessel, spacecraft, or planetary setting. The rolled theme is a fashion and cinematic-design language staged at that country location.

batchLayout.scenesOneAndTwo: Country-led hybrid. Across each image, two or three characters must wear hard, large, unmistakable country-motif couture. At least two characters must visibly carry the active thematic construction language. One or more hybrid looks may satisfy both requirements. Country motif and theme must both be foreground reads, not tiny trim or background-only cues.
batchLayout.scenesThreeAndFour: Theme-led original. All four characters wear structurally distinct outfits driven by the active unrelated cinematic theme, staged at two additional original locations in the current country. Do not force map-print country outfits onto these two scenes, but keep the recognizable country landmark equally foregrounded with the thematic fashion.
batchLayout.themeDuration: Hold each active cinematic theme for two complete country batches, then advance once to the next theme. Both theme-led scenes in a batch use the same active theme but must have different outfit fingerprints, contact graphs, and movement verbs.

cinematicThemeRotation.themeLocationFusion: Compose the active theme and country location as one authored scene. Use theme-specific silhouette engineering, materials, accessories, lighting language, route-map design, and movement while keeping the landmark large, recognizable, and unobscured. Reject generic country backdrops with pasted-on themed clothing and reject themed sets that erase the country.

themeExamples.helicopter: Use rotor-radial pleats, aerodynamic wrap structures, landing-skid heel architecture, cockpit-glass color blocking, and civilian flight-design cues without pilot impersonation or copied uniforms.
themeExamples.coastGuardVessel: Use fictional civilian rescue and conservation-vessel design language, wave-cut panels, flotation-inspired sculpting, deck-line tailoring, and marine visibility accents without official insignia, badges, copied uniforms, raids, rescue emergencies, or threats.
themeExamples.spaceAndPlanetary: Use fictional couture inspired by pressure-shell geometry, regolith texture, orbital arcs, solar shielding, rover joints, and mission-light systems. Keep all scenes public-safe fashion at the current country landmark. Near-Sun means a fictional shielded solar-observation design language, never a literal person standing on the Sun.

cinematicThemeRotation.publicSafety: Use fictional public-safe fashion references only. No copied airline, military, police, coast-guard, space-agency, or emergency-service uniforms or insignia. No combat, raids, arrests, threats, injury, emergency peril, fetish framing, or explicit content.

anatomyIntegrity.limbCount: In standard scenes render exactly four adult characters with exactly two arms and two hands per character, eight arms and eight hands total. In the selected male-model scene render exactly five adult characters with exactly two arms and two hands per character, ten arms and ten hands total. Every character also has anatomically correct legs and feet. Never create an extra, duplicated, floating, fused, borrowed, ownerless, or partially emerging hand, arm, finger cluster, leg, or foot.
anatomyIntegrity.contactClarity: Every affectionate contact must have an unambiguous owner. Trace each visible arm continuously from shoulder through elbow and wrist to one hand. Keep overlapping hugs readable through clean silhouettes and natural occlusion.
anatomyIntegrity.acceptanceGate: Before accepting an image, audit every character one by one for correct arm and hand count, plausible joints, five natural fingers where visible, and clear ownership of every touching hand. Require eight total hands in a four-person scene and ten total hands in the selected five-person scene, allowing only natural occlusion. Reject or use the single allowed recovery pass when any extra or ambiguous hand appears.
